extracted.intended_audience: PRSA members and public relations professionals
extracted.subtask_short: PRSA Code of Ethics for PR professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Official PRSA Code of Ethics and BEPS position papers describing core professional values, provisions of conduct, and topic-specific ethical guidance for public relations practice. Used to evaluate and guide ethical behavior across PR activities, including media relations, social media, influencers, AI, and commercial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent. We provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value that should guide conduct and decisions; applied across communications to support informed public debate and stakeholder decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires accuracy and truthfulness in all communications; underpins multiple Code provisions (e.g., Free Flow of Information, Disclosure). Examples of improper conduct (e.g., lying by omission) violate this value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience. We advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entails ongoing professional development, using specialized knowledge responsibly, and advancing credibility and relationships with institutions and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires objective counsel, accountability, and avoidance of actions that compromise professional judgment or create conflicts with the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance client/employer loyalty with public interest obligations; informs handling of confidential information and conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public. We respect all opinions and support the right of free expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires fair treatment of all stakeholders; informs practices around competition, intellectual property, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Protecting and advancing the free flow of accurate and truthful information is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: maintain integrity of relationships with media, government, and the public. Guidelines: Preserve integrity of communication processes; be honest and accurate; act promptly to correct erroneous communications; preserve free flow when giving/receiving gifts by ensuring gifts are nominal, legal, and infrequent. Examples of improper conduct provided (e.g., giving expensive gifts to influence coverage; entertaining officials beyond legal limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: promote respect and fair competition. Guidelines: Follow ethical hiring practices that respect free and open competition without deliberately undermining a competitor; preserve intellectual property rights. Examples of improper conduct (e.g., sharing helpful competitive information with one firm; spreading unfounded rumors to recruit business).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Open communication fosters informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build trust by revealing all information needed for responsible decision making. Guidelines: Be honest and accurate; act promptly to correct errors; investigate truthfulness of information released; reveal sponsors for causes/interests; disclose financial interests (e.g., stock ownership); avoid deceptive practices. Examples of improper conduct include front groups, lying by omission, failing to correct inaccuracies, and employing people to pose as volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Client trust requires appropriate protection of confidential and private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: protect privacy rights of clients, organizations, and individuals. Guidelines: Safeguard confidences and privacy rights of present, former, and prospective clients and employees; protect privileged, confidential, or insider information; immediately advise appropriate authority if confidential information is being divulged by an employee. Examples: taking confidential information to a new job and using it to the detriment of a former employer; intentionally leaking proprietary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Avoiding real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest builds the trust of clients, employers, and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: earn trust by avoiding/ending situations that put personal/professional interests in conflict with society's interests. Guidelines: Act in the best interests of client/employer even subordinating personal interests; avoid actions that may appear to compromise judgment; disclose promptly any existing or potential conflicts to affected clients/organizations; encourage clients/customers to determine if a conflict exists after notification. Examples of improper conduct: failing to disclose strong financial interest in a competitor; representing a competitor without informing prospective client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Public relations professionals work constantly to strengthen the public’s trust in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build respect and credibility and improve/adapt practices. Guidelines: Acknowledge obligation to protect/enhance the profession; keep informed and educated about practices; actively pursue professional development; decline representation that urges actions contrary to the Code; accurately define what PR activities can accomplish; counsel and require subordinates to adhere to the Code; report practices failing to comply with the Code. Examples of improper conduct include making public claims without evidence or assigning questionable work to non-members to avoid obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-Play (position & avoidance guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay-for-play: transactions in which payor makes undisclosed payments to a media channel to feature content, deceiving consumers into believing content was selected on merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: pay-for-play conflicts with Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. How to avoid: request and include disclosure when compensation provided in return for exposure; encourage journalists/bloggers/digital operators to disclose free or special travel, lodging, gifts or non-monetary compensation; encourage clear and obvious disclosure of crucial information consumers should have or expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics & Social Media (use of social platforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because social platforms are broad, fast, and largely unregulated, PR practitioners must incorporate a higher standard of practice by adhering to the PRSA Code of Ethics in all social media strategies, tactics and utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: do not accept common social media practices at face value; apply Disclosure of Information (disclose paid placements and associations), Safeguarding Confidences (protect confidential info), Conflicts of Interest (disclose conflicts; require proper FTC disclosures for influencers; gifts must be nominal/legal/infrequent), and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendation: understand trust is currency on social media; ensure disclosures are clear, and be cognizant of employee free speech rights (NLRB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (definition and avoidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is the unauthorized use or close imitation of the language and thoughts of another and representing that content as your own original work; it can be inadvertent or intentional and may be treated as fraud or theft of intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: inadvertent violation carries equal weight to intentional misrepresentation. How to avoid: do not copy content (sentence, paragraph, document) and present it as your own; use your own words and paraphrase; give proper credit when paraphrasing; use quotation marks and credit the source for exact wording; disclose all sources; when using internet sources, recognize creators are entitled to credit and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Spokespersons and Influencers (disclosure requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone paid to serve as a spokesperson, advocate or influencer for an organization must disclose the contractual arrangement or relationship between the spokesperson and the sponsor providing compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: such paid relationships implicate Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. How to maintain ethical standards: commercial relationships must be disclosed in advance of or simultaneous to the public forum; every party has obligation to disclose; be honest and accurate; reveal sponsors and any financial interest that may affect outcomes; failure to disclose is improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups (prohibition and transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: A front group is created or labeled to mislead the public about its true mission; assisting front groups or individuals representing undisclosed sponsorships or deceptive descriptions constitutes improper conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: deception violates the Code (Free Flow of Information, Disclosure, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession). How to maintain ethics: recognize assisting front groups—even if lawful—constitutes improper conduct and should be avoided; prioritize transparency and open communication essential for informed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Fees or Compensation (billing integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging clients for work not performed or overstating charges, fees or compensation is unethical and harms the profession; members should charge clients only for services rendered and in accordance with contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: violates Enhancing the Profession and professional values like Honesty. Guidelines: proper reporting of services rendered, time spent, out-of-pocket charges, and related fees; do not inflate charges or related support data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising & Sponsored Content (clear distinction & disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsored or native content should be clearly distinguishable from organic content; sponsors should be clearly identified to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: the sponsor should be clearly identified; this implicates Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Competition, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: ensure sponsorship is fully disclosed in context; disclosures should be clear and appropriate to the medium; sponsored content must be easily discernable and must not attempt to deceive consumers into believing content is independent or objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Leadership Accountabilities (machine decision accountability)
rubrics_metrics.description: When AI or machine learning systems make decisions, accountability should rest with human beings with oversight responsibility at the time the errant decision is made; organizations and leaders are expected to identify root causes and corrective actions with transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: machines cannot be held accountable; human oversight must be assigned. How to address: counsel senior leadership that AI processes cannot be held accountable and human beings charged with active oversight hold ownership; when developing communications about AI decisions, draw clear lines of human responsibility and present them forthrightly; applicable Code provisions include Disclosure, Free Flow, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media as a Reflection of Majority Opinion (representativeness caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media activity is not a scientifically vetted indicator of majority public opinion and may not represent the majority; a small fraction of users often drive the majority of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: communicators should remind audiences that social media sources are informal and may not accurately represent majority sentiment. When sharing analysis based on social media, present it as non-scientific, contextualize limitations, and avoid overstating representativeness. Applicable Code provisions: Free Flow, Disclosure, Enhancing the Profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Leaks (confidentiality and organizational obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should refrain from leaking information to media or stakeholders without expressed approval of organizational leadership; leaks undermine trust and may be illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS Position: leaking undermines the profession and can carry criminal or civil penalties. How to adhere: be aware of laws, regulations, contracts, NDAs and business terms governing information flow; adhere to contractual and legal obligations; never share information obtained in confidence without authorization; follow procedures for approving disclosures to internal and external publics. Applicable Code provisions: Safeguarding Confidence, Disclosure, Free Flow, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession.
